approved_classes.ex:AminoAcid: Amino acids are the building blocks of proteins.
approved_classes.ex:ChemicalSubstance: A general class for substances with chemical properties, including amino acids.
approved_classes.ex:Protein: Proteins are made up of amino acids and are involved in various biological processes.
approved_classes.ex:EssentialAminoAcid: Amino acids that are not synthesized by the human body and must be obtained from food.
approved_classes.ex:SemiEssentialAminoAcid: Amino acids that can be produced by the body but may need to be supplemented in growing children.
approved_classes.ex:NonEssentialAminoAcid: Amino acids that can be synthesized by the human body and do not require dietary intake.
approved_classes.ex:AromaticAminoAcid: Amino acids with an aromatic ring in their structure, such as phenylalanine, tyrosine, and tryptophan.
approved_classes.ex:AliphaticAminoAcid: Amino acids with aliphatic side chains, including glycine, alanine, valine, leucine, isoleucine, etc.
approved_classes.ex:BranchedChainAminoAcid: A specific type of aliphatic amino acid with branched aliphatic side chains (leucine, isoleucine, valine).
approved_classes.ex:HydroxylGroupContainingAminoAcid: Amino acids containing a hydroxyl group in their structure, such as serine and threonine.
approved_classes.ex:SulphurContainingAminoAcid: Amino acids with sulfur-containing groups, specifically cysteine and methionine.
approved_classes.ex:BasicAminoAcid: Amino acids that are highly basic due to their guanidino group (lysine) or imidazole ring (arginine, histidine).
approved_classes.ex:AminoAcidWithAliphaticSideChain: A subclass of aliphatic amino acids with specific side chains.
approved_classes.ex:MonoamineMonocarboxylicAcid: A subclass of aliphatic amino acids that are simple monoamino monocarboxylic acids (glycine, alanine, valine, leucine, isoleucine).
approved_classes.ex:PurelyKetogenicAminoAcid: Amino acids that can be completely converted into ketone bodies during metabolism.
approved_classes.ex:KetogenicAndGlucogenicAminoAcid: Amino acids that have both ketogenic and glucogenic metabolic fates.
approved_classes.ex:PurelyGlucogenicAminoAcid: Amino acids that can be fully converted into glucose or glycogen during metabolism.
approved_classes.ex:NonPolarAminoAcid: Amino acids with non-polar side chains, also known as hydrophobic amino acids.
approved_classes.ex:PolarAminoAcidWithNoChargeOnRGroup: Amino acids with polar side chains but no net charge (glycine, serine, threonine, cysteine, glutamine, asparagine, tyrosine).
approved_classes.ex:PolarAminoAcidWithPositiveChargeOnRGr: Amino acids with polar side chains and a positive charge (lysine, arginine, histidine).
approved_classes.ex:PolarAminoAcidWithNegativeChargeOnRGr: Amino acids with polar side chains and a negative charge (aspartic acid, glutamic acid).
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Glycine: Produced by removing water and then adding cyanide to aldimine. Used in treating schizophrenia, stroke, sleep issues, BPH, metabolic syndrome, and a few uncommon inherited metabolic illnesses.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Alanine: Produced by removing water and then adding cyanide to aldimine. Used in boosting immunity and providing energy to the brain and central nervous system.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Valine: Produced by Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis. Commonly used in health supplements for muscle synthesis and maintenance, stress management, child growth, and immune system support.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Leucine: Produced by Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis. Increases physical performance or strength in the short term, prevents muscle loss, lowers blood glucose levels in type 2 diabetes.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Isoleucin: Produced by Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis. Required for children's growth and maintaining nitrogen balance in adults.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Norleucin: Produced by Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis. Artificial amino acid used to research protein structure and function, similar to Methionine.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Phenylala: Produced by removing water and then adding cyanide to aldimine. Used in treating depression, Parkinson's disease, multiple sclerosis, pain, acupuncture anesthesia, osteoarthritis.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Tyrosine: Produced by removing water and then adding cyanide to aldimine. Commonly used in the production of thyroid hormone. Helps with mental performance, alertness, and memory.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Serine: Produced by removing water and then adding cyanide to aldimine. Particularly significant for brain and central nervous system function.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Cysteine: Used in medicine to enhance the efficiency of corticosteroid medications. Used in treating surgery and trauma as L-Cystine.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Threonine: Produced by Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis. Used for treating spinal spasticity, multiple sclerosis, familial spastic paraparesis, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Methionin: Used to prevent and cure depression, inflammation, liver illness, muscle discomfort. Used in weight loss, cholesterol reduction, and muscle development as Diiodothyronine.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Iodogorgi: Produced by treating an alpha halogenated acid ester with potassium phthalimide. Used in weight loss, cholesterol reduction, and muscle development as Diiodothyronine.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Thyroxine: Produced by treating an alpha halogenated acid ester with potassium phthalimide. Used in treating thyroid underactivity (hypothyroidism).
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Tryptopha: Used to treat anxiety and depression, migraines, headaches, and boosting growth hormone production.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Proline: Produced by Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis. Used for improving joint and skin health, muscle development, and injury healing.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Hydroxypr: Produced by removing water and then adding cyanide to aldimine. Required for collagen formation, the body's primary structural protein.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#AsparticA: Used in treating stress and exhaustion. Aids in energy generation from carbohydrates and RNA/DNA production.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Asparagin: Produced by removing water and then adding cyanide to aldimine. Necessary for brain development and function.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#GlutamicA: Used in treating Parkinson's, fatigue, and schizophrenia. Serves as a source of energy for the brain, improving clarity, alertness, and mood.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#BetaHydro: Produced by removing water and then adding cyanide to aldimine. Used in treating acne, photoaging, dry skin, psoriasis, melasma, fibromyalgia, dental scaling, and preventing urinary tract stones.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Glutamine: Used for maintaining blood sugar levels. Used in health supplements to support sports and performance, liver function, and wound healing.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Ornithine: Produced by Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis. Primarily used for supporting sports and performance, liver function, and wound healing.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Arginine: Used in treating cardiovascular disease due to its antiatherogenic, anti-ischemic, antiplatelet, and antithrombotic effects.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Lysine: Used for reducing cold sores when taken orally or applied as a cream. Used in treating anemia due to its presence in hemoglobin. Helps reduce blood pressure and is critical in baby feeding.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Histidine: Used for treating anemia, reducing blood pressure, and being critical in baby feeding as it is present in high percentages of hemoglobin.

ex:hasComposition.comment: Describes the composition of an amino acid as a chemical substance.

ex:isEssential.comment: Indicates whether an amino acid is essential.

ex:isSemiEssential.comment: Indicates whether an amino acid is semi-essential.

ex:isNonEssential.comment: Indicates whether an amino acid is non-essential.

ex:hasAliphaticSideChain.comment: Indicates whether an amino acid has aliphatic side chains.

ex:hasBranchedChain.comment: Indicates whether an amino acid is a branched-chain amino acid.

ex:hasAromaticRing.comment: Indicates whether an amino acid has an aromatic ring in its structure.

ex:hasHydroxylGroup.comment: Indicates whether an amino acid contains a hydroxyl group.

ex:hasSulphurGroup.comment: Indicates whether an amino acid has sulfur-containing groups.

ex:isBasic.comment: Indicates whether an amino acid is basic.

ex:hasAliphaticSideChainMonocarboxylicAc.comment: Indicates whether an amino acid has aliphatic side chains and is a monocarboxylic acid.

ex:isPurelyKetogenic.comment: Indicates whether an amino acid can be completely converted into ketone bodies.

ex:isKetogenicAndGlucogenic.comment: Indicates whether an amino acid has both ketogenic and glucogenic metabolic fates.

ex:isPurelyGlucogenic.comment: Indicates whether an amino acid can be fully converted into glucose or glycogen.

ex:hasNonPolarSideChain.comment: Indicates whether an amino acid has non-polar side chains (hydrophobic).

ex:hasPolarSideChainWithNoCharge.comment: Indicates whether an amino acid has polar side chains with no net charge.

ex:hasPolarSideChainWithPositiveCharge.comment: Indicates whether an amino acid has polar side chains with a positive charge.

ex:hasPolarSideChainWithNegativeCharge.comment: Indicates whether an amino acid has polar side chains with a negative charge.
